title: Map of Ancient Ephesus
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Hover over 27 numbered places on the site map of ancient Ephesus, from the Magnesian Gate to the Temple of Artemis and the hill of Ayasuluk, to see how the city, its harbor, and its later Christian and Turkish successors fit together, then test yourself in Quiz mode.

educational.topic: The site plan of ancient Ephesus
learningObjectives: The learner will locate the main sites of Ephesus on the site map and explain how the city's layout, from the silted harbor to the hill of Ayasuluk, records the order in which it was built, used, and abandoned.
prerequisites: The harbor silting, the Temple of Artemis, and the walk down Curetes Street, from [Chapter 10](../../chapters/10-ephesus-greco-roman-city/index.md).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Interactive exploration followed by retrieval practice
keyQuestions: Why is the harbor now a field?
Why do the later sites cluster on Ayasuluk?
commonMisconceptions: The Temple of Artemis stood inside the Roman city.
Ephesus was always a seaside city.
assessmentOpportunities: Quiz mode: identify each marked part from its description

controls.name: Explore
controls.description: Default mode: hover a marker or label to read about that place.

controls.name: Quiz
controls.description: Hides the labels and asks you to click the marker that matches each description.
